\chapter{The correspondence with the C code}\label{chap:correspondence}

The model is checked against ratpoints v3.1.1 (commit \texttt{1a998538dfa8}). The C files below are those of the library and \texttt{main.c}, whose parts that the command-line program does not mirror are to be excluded. Every line of code of them lies in at most one recorded range: a range is either modelled by the Lean declarations named, or excluded from the model with a reason. Each recorded range is checked against the text it had when it was reviewed.

\item \csource{find_points.c}{1194}{1609}: not yet recorded (193 lines of code)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{1619}{1623}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{1624}{1626}: not yet recorded (3 lines of code)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{1639}{1650}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.barrett}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.barrett}: natural numbers for the \texttt{unsigned long}s, the product \texttt{u m} exact as the 128-bit product of the C code, and the difference exact, which does not wrap since the quotient times \texttt{p} is at most \texttt{u} for \texttt{m ≤ (2 \textasciicircum{} 64 -{} 1) / p}; the obligation that \texttt{u} is below \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 64}, which the C type gives, a hypothesis of the lemma that the result is \texttt{u \% p} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.barrett\_eq}); the form with the 128-bit product, which the builds of the model compile (the compiler defines \texttt{\_\_SIZEOF\_INT128\_\_}, and \texttt{RP\_NO\_INT128} is not set), for the division \texttt{u \% p} of the other builds, which gives the same remainder.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{1652}{1655}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.hornerSteps}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.hornerSteps}: computed from \texttt{Ratpoints.maxBitsInPrime} as the macro computes it from \texttt{RATPOINTS\_MAX\_BITS\_IN\_PRIME}, with \texttt{64} for \texttt{LONG\_LENGTH}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{1683}{1697}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}: the prime \texttt{p} itself, for its index \texttt{pn} in the table \texttt{prime}; the table a fresh array of \texttt{p + 1} entries, for the integers that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer \texttt{int\_next} and hands back through \texttt{is\_f\_square\_p}, and the coefficients a fresh array returned with the entry, for the array \texttt{coeffs\_mod\_p} of its caller, which it fills; one loop over the residues, for the two loops of the two branches of the schedule of Horner's rule, between which \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.hornerBarrett} chooses for each residue; the residues with a square value are not counted, and the exit asks only whether one entry is true, which is the test on the count \texttt{np} and the entry \texttt{p}; the entry is made also when \texttt{f(a)} is a square for every residue and there is no point at infinity modulo \texttt{p}, where \texttt{examine\_prime} returns \texttt{0}, the moduli being an input of the model, and for both of its codes \texttt{1} and \texttt{2}, which only the choice of the moduli tells apart, with the density and the fields of \texttt{prec\_entry} (stage I); the entry is a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and returned, where \texttt{examine\_prime} stores it in the field \texttt{ssp} of \texttt{prec\_entry}; it keeps only \texttt{p}, the table and the inverses (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry}), and no rows: those of the sieve entry of the prime (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.rows}) are made from it when they are first needed, also the row of \texttt{0}, which \texttt{examine\_prime} installs from the build; the fields \texttt{init}, \texttt{nf} and \texttt{pw} that \texttt{examine\_prime} sets (lines 1800 and 1817) and its reciprocal \texttt{magic} (line 1808) are those of the sieve entry of the prime (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry}), of which the prime is the single factor, made by \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}, which sets the reciprocal there, and so are the bias \texttt{bias} and the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaLength} (lines 1815 and 1816), which \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?} sets there with the formulas of these lines; no density \texttt{r} (line 1811), which serves the choice of the moduli (stage I).)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{1745}{1749}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}: the prime \texttt{p} itself, for its index \texttt{pn} in the table \texttt{prime}; the table a fresh array of \texttt{p + 1} entries, for the integers that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer \texttt{int\_next} and hands back through \texttt{is\_f\_square\_p}, and the coefficients a fresh array returned with the entry, for the array \texttt{coeffs\_mod\_p} of its caller, which it fills; one loop over the residues, for the two loops of the two branches of the schedule of Horner's rule, between which \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.hornerBarrett} chooses for each residue; the residues with a square value are not counted, and the exit asks only whether one entry is true, which is the test on the count \texttt{np} and the entry \texttt{p}; the entry is made also when \texttt{f(a)} is a square for every residue and there is no point at infinity modulo \texttt{p}, where \texttt{examine\_prime} returns \texttt{0}, the moduli being an input of the model, and for both of its codes \texttt{1} and \texttt{2}, which only the choice of the moduli tells apart, with the density and the fields of \texttt{prec\_entry} (stage I); the entry is a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and returned, where \texttt{examine\_prime} stores it in the field \texttt{ssp} of \texttt{prec\_entry}; it keeps only \texttt{p}, the table and the inverses (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry}), and no rows: those of the sieve entry of the prime (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.rows}) are made from it when they are first needed, also the row of \texttt{0}, which \texttt{examine\_prime} installs from the build; the fields \texttt{init}, \texttt{nf} and \texttt{pw} that \texttt{examine\_prime} sets (lines 1800 and 1817) and its reciprocal \texttt{magic} (line 1808) are those of the sieve entry of the prime (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry}), of which the prime is the single factor, made by \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}, which sets the reciprocal there, and so are the bias \texttt{bias} and the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaLength} (lines 1815 and 1816), which \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?} sets there with the formulas of these lines; no density \texttt{r} (line 1811), which serves the choice of the moduli (stage I).)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}: the entry of every modulus made here, by its factors computed again from \texttt{m} (\texttt{Ratpoints.modulusFactors}), where \texttt{make\_modulus} reads the codes \texttt{fac} of the factors and their number \texttt{nf} that \texttt{add\_moduli} stores with the candidate (lines 2405-2406), and where \texttt{sieving\_info} takes the entry of a prime from the loop of the tables (\texttt{prec[n].ssp}) and makes those of the prime powers and the products by \texttt{make\_modulus}; the primes and prime powers as factors of the entry, for the fields \texttt{nf}, \texttt{pw} and \texttt{factor} and the entries of the prime powers that \texttt{make\_power} makes; the tables of a prime power (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Factor.power}) computed for each modulus that needs them, where \texttt{add\_moduli} examines a prime power once, when the factorization of the first candidate that reaches it needs it (the power itself), whether or not that candidate is then offered, and keeps its tables in its buffer \texttt{pws} by its index (\texttt{pw\_idx}, lines 2350-2354, 2358-2359 and 2387-2394, with the count \texttt{npw} of line 2548), and \texttt{make\_modulus} makes the entry of a prime power once and keeps it by its index (\texttt{power\_se}); the tables of a prime power computed also when they say nothing, where \texttt{add\_moduli} refuses a modulus with such a factor (line 2395), and a prime factor whose prime says nothing (\texttt{examine\_prime} returns \texttt{0}, and \texttt{prime\_se[pn]} stays \texttt{NULL}) taken with its table from the loop of the tables, where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers no composite with such a factor (line 2383); a prime beyond those of the loop of the tables examined, with the exit, when the entry of a modulus needs it, where \texttt{sieving\_info} examines the primes from \texttt{prime[pn\_lim]} on, in the order of the table, with the exit, in the loop of the tables while its first two stages want more primes (lines 2693-2705; there they also give forbidden divisors) and for the third stage (lines 2976-3016), both only when the number of primes was left to the library (lines 2693 and 2980), also those that it then skips, and \texttt{add\_moduli} makes composites, prime powers and products alike, of the primes of the loop of the tables only (line 2370): the output does not depend on the primes examined, since the exit is taken only when the curve has no points; every modulus of the parameters taken, any product of powers of primes of the table below \texttt{Ratpoints.maxPrimeEven} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Params.WF}), where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers a composite only for an odd \texttt{9 ≤ m ≤ RATPOINTS\_COMPOSITE\_MAX} (line 2361; \texttt{ratpoints.h:210-{}211}, 64 by default) whose table is not too dear for the run (line 2368), with room in the buffer of the prime powers for its new prime powers (lines 2351 and 2390), a density \texttt{r < 1} (line 2402) and at most \texttt{RP\_MAX\_MODULI} candidates (line 2403), restrictions that the model lifts as choices of the moduli (stage I); the reciprocal \texttt{magic}, the bias \texttt{bias} and the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of every kind of modulus set here, with the formulas of the C code, where \texttt{examine\_prime} sets those of a prime with its table (lines 1808, 1815 and 1816), \texttt{make\_power} those of a prime power (lines 2422, 2424 and 2425) and \texttt{make\_modulus} those of a product (lines 2454, 2456 and 2457), the inverse of a prime read from its table, as from the table \texttt{inverses[pn]} of the build; natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s of these formulas; the inverses \texttt{dinv} empty, which the row offsets of the packing fill (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.classOffsets}); no density \texttt{r} (stage I), and no field \texttt{init}, the rows of every kind being made by one function (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.row}); the entry a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{make\_power} and \texttt{make\_modulus} take from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and the exit as \texttt{none}, for the prime that \texttt{sieving\_info} returns.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2503}{2503}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2522}{2532}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}: the arguments that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the word \texttt{den\_bits} and the classes \texttt{cls}) are not modelled, nor that choice (stage I): the moduli and their stages are those of the parameters, and the primes examined in the loop of the tables their first \texttt{P.examined}, beyond which \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?} examines a prime when a modulus needs it; the sieve entries of every modulus made here, those of the third stage included, which \texttt{sieving\_info} puts into \texttt{sieve\_list} in the choice of the third stage (line 3014), and again, sorted by density with the reserve of \texttt{adapt\_primes}, after it (lines 3026-3030; stage I), and the reciprocals of the entries of the moduli, where \texttt{sieving\_info} collects those of the reserve too (stage I); the flag \texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHECK\_DENOM} as the switch \texttt{checkDenom}, which the search clears, with the flag, when there is no forbidden divisor and no Jacobi test (\texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}); the sieve entries and the forbidden divisors returned as lists and the reciprocals as an array, for the arrays \texttt{sieve\_list} and \texttt{magics} and the arrays of the arguments, with no bound \texttt{2 RATPOINTS\_NUM\_PRIMES} on the number of the entries and the reciprocals (lines 332-333 and 347), which ratpoints never reaches since each of its entries owns a prime, where well-formed parameters may repeat a modulus, and the exit as \texttt{none}, for the prime returned; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}, \texttt{RP\_PRIME\_STATS} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)

the primes and prime powers as factors of the entry, for the fields \texttt{nf}, \texttt{pw} and \texttt{factor} and the entries of the prime powers that \texttt{make\_power} makes; the tables of a prime power (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Factor.power}) computed for each modulus that needs them, where \texttt{add\_moduli} examines a prime power once, when the factorization of the first candidate that reaches it needs it (the power itself), whether or not that candidate is then offered, and keeps its tables in its buffer \texttt{pws} by its index (\texttt{pw\_idx}, lines 2350-2354, 2358-2359 and 2387-2394, with the count \texttt{npw} of line 2548), and \texttt{make\_modulus} makes the entry of a prime power once and keeps it by its index (\texttt{power\_se}); the tables of a prime power computed also when they say nothing, where \texttt{add\_moduli} refuses a modulus with such a factor (line 2395), and a prime factor whose prime says nothing (\texttt{examine\_prime} returns \texttt{0}, and \texttt{prime\_se[pn]} stays \texttt{NULL}) taken with its table from the loop of the tables, where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers no composite with such a factor (line 2383); a prime beyond those of the loop of the tables examined, with the exit, when the entry of a modulus needs it, where \texttt{sieving\_info} examines the primes from \texttt{prime[pn\_lim]} on, in the order of the table, with the exit, in the loop of the tables while its first two stages want more primes (lines 2693-2705; there they also give forbidden divisors) and for the third stage (lines 2976-3016), both only when the number of primes was left to the library (lines 2693 and 2980), also those that it then skips, and \texttt{add\_moduli} makes composites, prime powers and products alike, of the primes of the loop of the tables only (line 2370): the output does not depend on the primes examined, since the exit is taken only when the curve has no points; every modulus of the parameters taken, any product of powers of primes of the table below \texttt{Ratpoints.maxPrimeEven} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Params.WF}), where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers a composite only for an odd \texttt{9 ≤ m ≤ RATPOINTS\_COMPOSITE\_MAX} (line 2361; \texttt{ratpoints.h:210-{}211}, 64 by default) whose table is not too dear for the run (line 2368), with room in the buffer of the prime powers for its new prime powers (lines 2351 and 2390), a density \texttt{r < 1} (line 2402) and at most \texttt{RP\_MAX\_MODULI} candidates (line 2403), restrictions that the model lifts as choices of the moduli (stage I); the reciprocal \texttt{magic}, the bias \texttt{bias} and the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of every kind of modulus set here, with the formulas of the C code, where \texttt{examine\_prime} sets those of a prime with its table (lines 1808, 1815 and 1816), \texttt{make\_power} those of a prime power (lines 2422, 2424 and 2425) and \texttt{make\_modulus} those of a product (lines 2454, 2456 and 2457), the inverse of a prime read from its table, as from the table \texttt{inverses[pn]} of the build; natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s of these formulas; the inverses \texttt{dinv} empty, which the row offsets of the packing fill (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.classOffsets}); no density \texttt{r} (stage I), and no field \texttt{init}, the rows of every kind being made by one function (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.row}); the entry a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{make\_power} and \texttt{make\_modulus} take from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and the exit as \texttt{none}, for the prime that \texttt{sieving\_info} returns.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2561}{2562}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.forbidden}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.forbidden}: the position \texttt{examined} as an argument, for the final \texttt{pn\_lim} of the loop of the tables; the Kronecker symbol by the table of the squares modulo \texttt{p}, which marks \texttt{0} as a square, for \texttt{mpz\_kronecker\_si}; the flag \texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHECK\_DENOM} not tested, since the search computes the forbidden divisors only when the flag is set, for even degree (\texttt{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}); lists, for the two arrays of the arguments with their terminating zeros; the words of a prime made with its entry, for the pointers into \texttt{sieves0} and the buffer \texttt{forb\_words}, with no failure for lack of memory, where \texttt{sieving\_info} drops the primes beyond the table whose words it cannot store; no reciprocals \texttt{magic}, which ratpoints reads only for the first word of a block (stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s; no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2566}{2566}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2793}{2795}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}: the arguments of \texttt{sieving\_info} that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the 2-adic classes and the word \texttt{den\_bits}) are not modelled; the denominators from \texttt{1} to \texttt{H}, for the range \texttt{b\_low, …, b\_high} (stage H); the flags of the denominators as Booleans, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags}; the forbidden divisors and the divisors of the leading coefficient with their records as lists, for the arrays \texttt{args-{}>forb\_ba}, \texttt{args-{}>forbidden}, \texttt{args-{}>den\_info} and \texttt{args-{}>divisors} of the arguments, and the sieve entries as a list, for the array \texttt{args-{}>sieve\_list} that \texttt{sieving\_info} fills and \texttt{class\_offsets} reads; the square test \texttt{lcfsq} of line 4906 made on the polynomial searched (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.isSquare}), where the C code computes it before the reversal check (line 4634) and clears it in case 2 (line 4770): the same value for an even degree, the only one that reads it; the test on \texttt{point\_at\_infty} of the 2-adic exit recomputed, as \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity} decides it; the exits give the empty list, where \texttt{sieving\_info} returns the prime and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} the number \texttt{0} of points found; the Sturm step does not restrict the search region before stage H, so that the return when it leaves nothing to search is never taken, and the run always follows the points at infinity; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; the array of the row offsets made with zeros, for the array on the stack, whose entries the C code leaves unset until \texttt{class\_offsets} writes them, with one offset in each row for each sieve entry of the run, those of its three stages, for the \texttt{sp3\_max} entries with the reserve of further primes (stage I); no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2801}{2801}: excluded (memory): the enlargement of ba\_buffer for the primes that the loop of the tables of sieving\_info looked at beyond num\_primes, which fails only for lack of memory
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2808}{2808}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{3112}{3114}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}: every numerator from \texttt{-{}H} to \texttt{H}, for the intervals of the search region that the Sturm step keeps (stage H), returning at the first interval beyond \texttt{H} and skipping an empty one, whose ends \texttt{interval\_bits} computes and clips to the height bound (lines 3426-3427), with the form of \texttt{numerators\_to\_bits} that the whole line takes: the plain one, which \texttt{interval\_bits} takes (line 3432), when \texttt{exact\_bounds} finds the forms of the ends of an interval, for \texttt{H ≤ LONG\_MAX -{} 64} (lines 3332-3338), and otherwise the split one, which \texttt{interval\_bits\_exact} takes (line 3404) (stage H); the height bound converted to \texttt{Int64}, which is exact for \texttt{H < 2 \textasciicircum{} 63}, and the bits back to integers; the sieve specs, and with them the rows of the residues, made before the bits of the interval, where \texttt{sift} turns the interval into bits first and makes them (the flag \texttt{do\_setup}) once an interval of numerators is not empty, which for the whole line is at once and so before the test \texttt{low ≤ high} of the bits; the rows made by their thunks when they are first needed (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.setRows}), for the test for the rows that are missing and their construction by the function \texttt{init} of the entry under the lock of the tables, which threads share; the end \texttt{sp1} of the first stage, the reciprocals \texttt{mgs} of the first two stages, the entries \texttt{es3} of the third stage and their reciprocals \texttt{mgs3} as arguments, for the numbers \texttt{sp1}, \texttt{sp2} and \texttt{sp3} that the sieving thread keeps (\texttt{worker\_init}), the array \texttt{magics} of the arguments, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} reads, and the entries \texttt{sieve\_list[sp2], …, sieve\_list[sp3 -{} 1]} and the reciprocals \texttt{magics[sp2], …, magics[sp3 -{} 1]}, which \texttt{fill\_checks} reads, with no correction of \texttt{sp2} and \texttt{sp3} between the blocks of the run (stage I); the residues \texttt{bp} and the class \texttt{cl} as values, for the pointers \texttt{bp\_list} and \texttt{cls}, and the array \texttt{offsets} of the row offsets of the run as an argument, which the C code reaches through the pointer \texttt{offset} of the class; the thunk of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.fillChecks}, for the table \texttt{checks} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{fill\_checks} fills, and its flag \texttt{stage3\_filled}, which \texttt{sift} clears; the thunk of the products \texttt{w}, for the flag \texttt{compute\_bc}, which \texttt{sift} sets and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} clears when it computes the products; no count of the denominators sieved (\texttt{n\_sifts}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli between the blocks of the run (stage I); a list of points, for the callback \texttt{process} with its argument \texttt{info} and for the count \texttt{total} of points that \texttt{sift} returns, with no stop that \texttt{process} may request (\texttt{quit}, which \texttt{worker\_init} clears, stage G); the arguments of the run passed explicitly, for the pointer \texttt{args} of the sieving thread (\texttt{rp-{}private.h:574}), which \texttt{worker\_init} sets and through which \texttt{sift} reads them; no search intervals \texttt{iv} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{worker\_init} clears (\texttt{find\_points.c:3130}) and \texttt{run\_block} sets for each block (\texttt{rp-{}private.h:574}; stage H); no pool, slot and stop flag of a thread of the pool, the flag by which the pool of threads tells it to abandon its block (\texttt{pool}, \texttt{slot}, \texttt{stop}, \texttt{rp-{}private.h:584-{}585}; stage I); natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; no measurements of the phases (\texttt{RP\_SIFT\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_SETUP\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_INIT\_TIC} and their \texttt{TOC}) and no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.siftPiece}: a fresh array of zeros for each piece, for the survivors array of the sieving thread, which every piece reuses, with one bit array more for the alignment, and whose words \texttt{malloc} leaves uninitialized; the piece by its first word number \texttt{w0} and its number \texttt{n} of bit arrays, for \texttt{w\_low} and \texttt{w\_high}, and an index for the pointer to its last bit array; the moduli of the first two stages with their rows and offsets as the list \texttt{specs} and the end \texttt{sp1} of the first stage, for the sieve specs \texttt{sieves} and the number \texttt{sp1} that the sieving thread keeps, the reciprocals of their moduli as the list \texttt{mgs}, for the array \texttt{magics} of the arguments, and the thunk \texttt{checks}, for the table \texttt{checks} of the third stage and its length \texttt{nchecks = sp3 -{} sp2}; the class \texttt{cl} as a value, for the pointer \texttt{cls}; integers for the \texttt{long}s of the test \texttt{small}, which stay \texttt{long}s, and a Boolean for its \texttt{int}; no count of the words of the piece (\texttt{n\_words}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli between the blocks of the run (stage I); the thunk \texttt{w} of the products of the check as an argument, where \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} computes the products when the first survivor of \texttt{b} reaches it; a list of points, for the callback \texttt{process} with its argument \texttt{info} and for the count \texttt{total} of points that \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} returns, with no flag \texttt{quit} for a stop that \texttt{process} may request (stage G); natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; no measurements of the phases (\texttt{RP\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_TOC}, \texttt{RP\_PHASE\_TIMING}) and no stop after one of them (\texttt{RP\_STOP\_AFTER}).)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{3122}{3122}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.checkPoint}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.checkPoint}: the products \texttt{w} as a thunk, which the sieve of one denominator makes for each denominator (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}) and which is forced when the first numerator of \texttt{b} reaches the check, for the array \texttt{work} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{worker\_init} gives it, and its flag \texttt{compute\_bc}, which \texttt{sift} sets and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} clears when it computes the products; the degree \texttt{d} and the flag \texttt{rev} as arguments, handed down from \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.sieveRun} through the components that call the check, for the degree and the bit \texttt{RATPOINTS\_REVERSED} of the flags of the search, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} reads through its worker (\texttt{args-{}>degree}, \texttt{args-{}>flags}); a list of points, for the callback \texttt{process} and for the count of points that \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} returns, with no stop that \texttt{process} may request, and no \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_Y} and no \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} (stage G); integers for the \texttt{long}s \texttt{a} and \texttt{b} (the negations of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.swapPoint} stay \texttt{long}s by \texttt{Ratpoints.fitsLong\_neg}); no measurements of the time of the check and of its products (\texttt{RP\_CHECK}, \texttt{RP\_BC\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_BC\_TOC} under \texttt{RP\_PHASE\_TIMING}), and no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{3123}{3124}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}: every numerator from \texttt{-{}H} to \texttt{H}, for the intervals of the search region that the Sturm step keeps (stage H), returning at the first interval beyond \texttt{H} and skipping an empty one, whose ends \texttt{interval\_bits} computes and clips to the height bound (lines 3426-3427), with the form of \texttt{numerators\_to\_bits} that the whole line takes: the plain one, which \texttt{interval\_bits} takes (line 3432), when \texttt{exact\_bounds} finds the forms of the ends of an interval, for \texttt{H ≤ LONG\_MAX -{} 64} (lines 3332-3338), and otherwise the split one, which \texttt{interval\_bits\_exact} takes (line 3404) (stage H); the height bound converted to \texttt{Int64}, which is exact for \texttt{H < 2 \textasciicircum{} 63}, and the bits back to integers; the sieve specs, and with them the rows of the residues, made before the bits of the interval, where \texttt{sift} turns the interval into bits first and makes them (the flag \texttt{do\_setup}) once an interval of numerators is not empty, which for the whole line is at once and so before the test \texttt{low ≤ high} of the bits; the rows made by their thunks when they are first needed (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.setRows}), for the test for the rows that are missing and their construction by the function \texttt{init} of the entry under the lock of the tables, which threads share; the end \texttt{sp1} of the first stage, the reciprocals \texttt{mgs} of the first two stages, the entries \texttt{es3} of the third stage and their reciprocals \texttt{mgs3} as arguments, for the numbers \texttt{sp1}, \texttt{sp2} and \texttt{sp3} that the sieving thread keeps (\texttt{worker\_init}), the array \texttt{magics} of the arguments, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} reads, and the entries \texttt{sieve\_list[sp2], …, sieve\_list[sp3 -{} 1]} and the reciprocals \texttt{magics[sp2], …, magics[sp3 -{} 1]}, which \texttt{fill\_checks} reads, with no correction of \texttt{sp2} and \texttt{sp3} between the blocks of the run (stage I); the residues \texttt{bp} and the class \texttt{cl} as values, for the pointers \texttt{bp\_list} and \texttt{cls}, and the array \texttt{offsets} of the row offsets of the run as an argument, which the C code reaches through the pointer \texttt{offset} of the class; the thunk of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.fillChecks}, for the table \texttt{checks} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{fill\_checks} fills, and its flag \texttt{stage3\_filled}, which \texttt{sift} clears; the thunk of the products \texttt{w}, for the flag \texttt{compute\_bc}, which \texttt{sift} sets and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} clears when it computes the products; no count of the denominators sieved (\texttt{n\_sifts}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli between the blocks of the run (stage I); a list of points, for the callback \texttt{process} with its argument \texttt{info} and for the count \texttt{total} of points that \texttt{sift} returns, with no stop that \texttt{process} may request (\texttt{quit}, which \texttt{worker\_init} clears, stage G); the arguments of the run passed explicitly, for the pointer \texttt{args} of the sieving thread (\texttt{rp-{}private.h:574}), which \texttt{worker\_init} sets and through which \texttt{sift} reads them; no search intervals \texttt{iv} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{worker\_init} clears (\texttt{find\_points.c:3130}) and \texttt{run\_block} sets for each block (\texttt{rp-{}private.h:574}; stage H); no pool, slot and stop flag of a thread of the pool, the flag by which the pool of threads tells it to abandon its block (\texttt{pool}, \texttt{slot}, \texttt{stop}, \texttt{rp-{}private.h:584-{}585}; stage I); natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; no measurements of the phases (\texttt{RP\_SIFT\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_SETUP\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_INIT\_TIC} and their \texttt{TOC}) and no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4523}{4528}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), for the codes and the order of the library: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height} of the arguments (\texttt{ratpoints.h:362}), so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses; a height that is not a \texttt{long}, \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63} or more, is refused with error 4, as the program refuses it when it reads the height (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}), where the library cannot be given one, its height being a \texttt{long}. A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller (the reversed coefficients, the degree, the flags), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the points are returned as a list, for the count \texttt{total} and the flag \texttt{quit} of the callback (stage G); the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it, is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set. No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4542}{4545}: excluded (interface): the input fields of the arguments that find\_points\_work saves, so that a caller who reuses the arguments for the next curve does not find the normalizations and choices of the search in them; the model writes nothing back

the square test \texttt{lcfsq} of line 4906 made on the polynomial searched (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.isSquare}), where the C code computes it before the reversal check (line 4634) and clears it in case 2 (line 4770): the same value for an even degree, the only one that reads it; the test on \texttt{point\_at\_infty} of the 2-adic exit recomputed, as \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity} decides it; the exits give the empty list, where \texttt{sieving\_info} returns the prime and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} the number \texttt{0} of points found; the Sturm step does not restrict the search region before stage H, so that the return when it leaves nothing to search is never taken, and the run always follows the points at infinity; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; the array of the row offsets made with zeros, for the array on the stack, whose entries the C code leaves unset until \texttt{class\_offsets} writes them, with one offset in each row for each sieve entry of the run, those of its three stages, for the \texttt{sp3\_max} entries with the reserve of further primes (stage I); no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4577}{4577}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4578}{4585}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), for the codes and the order of the library: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height} of the arguments (\texttt{ratpoints.h:362}), so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses; a height that is not a \texttt{long}, \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63} or more, is refused with error 4, as the program refuses it when it reads the height (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}), where the library cannot be given one, its height being a \texttt{long}. A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller (the reversed coefficients, the degree, the flags), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the points are returned as a list, for the count \texttt{total} and the flag \texttt{quit} of the callback (stage G); the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it, is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set. No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)

without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4658}{4658}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), for the codes and the order of the library: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height} of the arguments (\texttt{ratpoints.h:362}), so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses; a height that is not a \texttt{long}, \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63} or more, is refused with error 4, as the program refuses it when it reads the height (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}), where the library cannot be given one, its height being a \texttt{long}. A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller (the reversed coefficients, the degree, the flags), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the points are returned as a list, for the count \texttt{total} and the flag \texttt{quit} of the callback (stage G); the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it, is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set. No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}: a new list for the reversal in place, and nothing written back to the caller: the reversed coefficients, the degree and the flag \texttt{RATPOINTS\_REVERSED} are returned instead; the switch for the test of the flags \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_REVERSE} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_REVERSE\_AUTO}, so that the check runs whenever the switch allows it, without \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_REVERSE\_AUTO}, which a search region or a denominator range sets (stage H); the square test of \texttt{c\_d} made here, where the C code reads the flag \texttt{lcfsq} that the set-up computes before (line 4634), and no flag \texttt{lcfsq} for the reversed list, which case 2 clears, since \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity} tests the leading coefficient of the list it is given; integers and their absolute values for the GMP integers, with no scratch integers \texttt{work[0]} and \texttt{work[1]}; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4894}{4899}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}: the flag \texttt{rev} as an argument, for the bit \texttt{RATPOINTS\_REVERSED} of the flags of the search (\texttt{args-{}>flags}); a list of points for the callback \texttt{process}, with no stop it may request, no \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_Y} and no \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} (stage G), and no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}; the square test of \texttt{c\_d} and the decision whether there are points at infinity are made on the list that it is given, after the reversal check, when the points are delivered, where the C code computes \texttt{lcfsq} before the check (line 4634), which clears it when it reverses a polynomial of even degree and leaves it, unread, with the odd degree of the other reversals, and sets \texttt{point\_at\_infty} before the exits of the search (lines 4894-4899); the case \texttt{c\_d = 0}, that of the zero polynomial, which ratpoints refuses before it gets here, gives the one point \texttt{(a, 0, b)}, which the cited lines, delivering \texttt{-{}y} without a test \texttt{y ≠ 0}, would deliver twice.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4900}{4943}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}: the arguments of \texttt{sieving\_info} that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the 2-adic classes and the word \texttt{den\_bits}) are not modelled; the denominators from \texttt{1} to \texttt{H}, for the range \texttt{b\_low, …, b\_high} (stage H); the flags of the denominators as Booleans, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags}; the forbidden divisors and the divisors of the leading coefficient with their records as lists, for the arrays \texttt{args-{}>forb\_ba}, \texttt{args-{}>forbidden}, \texttt{args-{}>den\_info} and \texttt{args-{}>divisors} of the arguments, and the sieve entries as a list, for the array \texttt{args-{}>sieve\_list} that \texttt{sieving\_info} fills and \texttt{class\_offsets} reads; the square test \texttt{lcfsq} of line 4906 made on the polynomial searched (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.isSquare}), where the C code computes it before the reversal check (line 4634) and clears it in case 2 (line 4770): the same value for an even degree, the only one that reads it; the test on \texttt{point\_at\_infty} of the 2-adic exit recomputed, as \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity} decides it; the exits give the empty list, where \texttt{sieving\_info} returns the prime and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} the number \texttt{0} of points found; the Sturm step does not restrict the search region before stage H, so that the return when it leaves nothing to search is never taken, and the run always follows the points at infinity; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; the array of the row offsets made with zeros, for the array on the stack, whose entries the C code leaves unset until \texttt{class\_offsets} writes them, with one offset in each row for each sieve entry of the run, those of its three stages, for the \texttt{sp3\_max} entries with the reserve of further primes (stage I); no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}: the arguments of \texttt{sieving\_info} that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the 2-adic classes and the word \texttt{den\_bits}) are not modelled; the denominators from \texttt{1} to \texttt{H}, for the range \texttt{b\_low, …, b\_high} (stage H); the flags of the denominators as Booleans, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags}; the forbidden divisors and the divisors of the leading coefficient with their records as lists, for the arrays \texttt{args-{}>forb\_ba}, \texttt{args-{}>forbidden}, \texttt{args-{}>den\_info} and \texttt{args-{}>divisors} of the arguments, and the sieve entries as a list, for the array \texttt{args-{}>sieve\_list} that \texttt{sieving\_info} fills and \texttt{class\_offsets} reads; the square test \texttt{lcfsq} of line 4906 made on the polynomial searched (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.isSquare}), where the C code computes it before the reversal check (line 4634) and clears it in case 2 (line 4770): the same value for an even degree, the only one that reads it; the test on \texttt{point\_at\_infty} of the 2-adic exit recomputed, as \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity} decides it; the exits give the empty list, where \texttt{sieving\_info} returns the prime and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} the number \texttt{0} of points found; the Sturm step does not restrict the search region before stage H, so that the return when it leaves nothing to search is never taken, and the run always follows the points at infinity; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; the array of the row offsets made with zeros, for the array on the stack, whose entries the C code leaves unset until \texttt{class\_offsets} writes them, with one offset in each row for each sieve entry of the run, those of its three stages, for the \texttt{sp3\_max} entries with the reserve of further primes (stage I); no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{5219}{5220}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), for the codes and the order of the library: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height} of the arguments (\texttt{ratpoints.h:362}), so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses; a height that is not a \texttt{long}, \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63} or more, is refused with error 4, as the program refuses it when it reads the height (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}), where the library cannot be given one, its height being a \texttt{long}. A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller (the reversed coefficients, the degree, the flags), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the points are returned as a list, for the count \texttt{total} and the flag \texttt{quit} of the callback (stage G); the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it, is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set. No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)

\section*{\texttt{sift.c}}
\begin{itemize}
\item \csource{sift.c}{30}{30}: excluded (other): the include of the private header; the model has no headers
\item \csource{sift.c}{55}{176}: excluded (instrumentation): RP\_PHASE\_TIMING and RP\_PHASE\_COUNTS, development instrumentation that times the parts of \_ratpoints\_sift0 with rdtsc, counts what survives each and prints one line on stderr at exit, with the arm of the production build, where the timers RP\_TIC and RP\_TOC are empty and RP\_CHECK is the call it wraps
\item \csource{sift.c}{194}{201}: excluded (instrumentation): RP\_STOP\_AFTER, development instrumentation that cuts the pipeline short after a step so that its cost can be measured, 0 in the production build, with the exact check of its level 4 replaced by a count

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.checkPoint}: the products \texttt{w} as a thunk, which the sieve of one denominator makes for each denominator (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}) and which is forced when the first numerator of \texttt{b} reaches the check, for the array \texttt{work} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{worker\_init} gives it, and its flag \texttt{compute\_bc}, which \texttt{sift} sets and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} clears when it computes the products; the degree \texttt{d} and the flag \texttt{rev} as arguments, handed down from \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.sieveRun} through the components that call the check, for the degree and the bit \texttt{RATPOINTS\_REVERSED} of the flags of the search, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} reads through its worker (\texttt{args-{}>degree}, \texttt{args-{}>flags}); a list of points, for the callback \texttt{process} and for the count of points that \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} returns, with no stop that \texttt{process} may request, and no \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_Y} and no \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} (stage G); integers for the \texttt{long}s \texttt{a} and \texttt{b} (the negations of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.swapPoint} stay \texttt{long}s by \texttt{Ratpoints.fitsLong\_neg}); no measurements of the time of the check and of its products (\texttt{RP\_CHECK}, \texttt{RP\_BC\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_BC\_TOC} under \texttt{RP\_PHASE\_TIMING}), and no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)
\item \csource{sift.c}{207}{213}: excluded (instrumentation): the sink into which the levels of RP\_STOP\_AFTER accumulate the work they leave out, printed on stderr at exit
\item \csource{sift.c}{225}{238}: excluded (instrumentation): RP\_MOD\_CHOICE, a development switch that chooses the reduction of the word numbers of the chunked first stage at run time, from the environment variable RP\_MOD\_MUL, so that the two reductions can be timed in one binary; in the production build RP\_USE\_MOD\_MUL is the constant 1, the reduction by the reciprocal wherever it is exact

\section*{\texttt{init.c}}
\begin{itemize}
\item \csource{init.c}{30}{30}: excluded (other): the include of the private header; the model has no headers
\item \csource{init.c}{42}{46}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry.admits}, \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.row}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry.admits}: the bit of \texttt{a} in the row of \texttt{r}, computed from the tables for each numerator, where ratpoints builds the row of a residue \texttt{r ≠ 0} once, when a denominator first needs it, as a bit pattern of \texttt{p} bits repeated through words, by a function for each prime that the build generates, and takes the row of \texttt{0} from the pattern \texttt{sieves0} that the build generates, whose bit \texttt{N} is clear exactly when \texttt{p} divides \texttt{N}.)
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.row}: one function for every kind of modulus, the pattern of one period from \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.admits} laid out in words by windows into its packed form, as \texttt{lay\_out\_pattern} lays out the pattern of a prime power, for the builders of the rows of a prime in \texttt{init.c}, which step through the residues \texttt{a b⁻¹ mod p} four at a time and rotate the pattern through the words, one function for each prime that the build generates, for the pattern \texttt{sieves0} that the build generates for the row of \texttt{0} of a prime, and for the row of a product, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sieve\_init\_product} lays down from the rows of its factors (stage F4); in \texttt{lay\_out\_pattern}, the packed pattern made bit by bit, where it is or-ed together from shifted copies of the pattern, the position of each window computed, where it is stepped by \texttt{64 mod p}, and the first \texttt{p} words repeated, where all \texttt{p rbaPack} are computed; a fresh array, for the space that the builders take from the buffer of the tables (\texttt{ba\_next}), and the row returned, where the builders also store it in the field \texttt{sieve} of the entry, with a release store for the threads (\texttt{RP\_PUBLISH}), which the thunks of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.rows} do; the copies of the first bit arrays that the builders append at the end of a row, which only the chunked first stage reads, are none in the build of the model (\texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHUNK} = 1; stage F4).)

\section*{\texttt{sturm.c}}
\begin{itemize}
\item \csource{sturm.c}{29}{97}: not yet recorded (29 lines of code)
\item \csource{sturm.c}{99}{163}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.chain}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.chain}: the rows as arrays of their coefficients up to their degree, for the table of \texttt{(d + 1)\textasciicircum{}2} GMP integers and the array of degrees, with no \texttt{mpz\_init} and \texttt{mpz\_clear} (a chain has at most \texttt{d + 1} rows, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sturm.IsChain.size\_le}, and its row \texttt{k + 1} at most \texttt{d -{} k} entries, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sturm.IsChain.size\_getElem!\_add\_one\_add\_le}): an array has one entry more than the degree of its row, and a remainder that becomes zero is the empty array, where the degree in the C code reaches \texttt{-{}1}; a reduction step drops the leading coefficient, which it makes \texttt{0}, where the C code lowers the degree; the rows are handed back, and \texttt{none} for the return of \texttt{-{}1}, where \texttt{\_ratpoints\_compute\_sturm} keeps them in its table for the rest of the Sturm step (stage H), and the index of the last row, which the C code leaves in \texttt{k} and sets to \texttt{d} after the loop for \texttt{d = 1}, is the size of the array less one; a list of integers for the array of GMP integers of the coefficients, local values for the scratch integers \texttt{work[0]}, \texttt{work[1]} and \texttt{work[2]}, and Lean's \texttt{/} for \texttt{mpz\_fdiv\_q}, which agree on the divisions of the chain, all exact.)
\item \csource{sturm.c}{166}{332}: not yet recorded (136 lines of code)
\end{itemize}

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.rbaLength}: computed from \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack}, where each build sets \texttt{RBA\_LENGTH} by a literal, and its logarithm \texttt{RBA\_SHIFT} too (\texttt{Ratpoints.rbaShift}); the shifts by \texttt{RBA\_SHIFT} and by \texttt{LONG\_SHIFT} are divisions by \texttt{rbaLength} and by 64, which round down also for a negative value, as the arithmetic shifts of gcc do, and the masks by \texttt{RBA\_LENGTH -{} 1} and by \texttt{LONG\_MASK} Euclidean remainders.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{55}{58}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.rbaPack}
